title: Trades on Record
transcript: A retired umbrella repairer arrived at a town library carrying a small box of metal tips. The librarian had invited him to record how he repaired umbrellas because the town's last repair stall was about to close. During the recording, he kept saying things like this end and that notch. When volunteers listened back, they could follow his story but could barely tell which part he was holding. For later sessions, they photographed each object as it was discussed and linked the photographs to the relevant moments in the recording. A vocational teacher who tried the archive used one interview to show students how a repairer chose among several nearly identical parts. The library now asks each guest to bring in an unfinished job.

questions.prompt: What did the volunteers find difficult when listening to the recording?
options: Working out when the repair took place
Identifying the parts the repairer was referring to
Understanding why the repairer had retired
questions.answer: Identifying the parts the repairer was referring to
questions.explanation: 录音里多次出现“这一端”之类的说法，志愿者难以辨认具体部件。

questions.prompt: Why does the library most likely ask guests to bring unfinished jobs?
options: To help them estimate the time each job takes
To collect objects that can be displayed permanently
To let visitors try completing the jobs themselves
To capture the practical choices workers make as they demonstrate their trade
questions.answer: To capture the practical choices workers make as they demonstrate their trade
questions.explanation: 带来未完成的活儿，便于现场演示手艺人怎样选择部件和处理实际问题。
